    pass

examples.explanation: At 4 pages per hour the documents take 1 + 2 + 2 + 3 = 8 hours. At 3 they'd take 10.
With one hour per document, the speed must cover the largest one.

steps.title: Clarify the input
steps.description: Confirms the printer works on one document per hour and doesn't carry leftover capacity to the next document.
look_for: asks whether the printer can split an hour between documents
mentions h at least the number of documents
hints: Before you start, is there anything about how the printer spends an hour that you'd want to confirm?
If a document finishes halfway through an hour, can the printer start the next one?
Confirm each hour goes to one document, so a document takes pages over speed hours, rounded up.

steps.title: Count the hours for a given speed
steps.description: Computes the total hours needed at a speed using rounded-up division.
hints: Look at how many hours one document takes at a given speed.
If a document has 7 pages at 4 pages per hour, is that 1.75 hours or 2?
Each document takes its pages divided by the speed, rounded up; add those up.

steps.title: Search over the speed
steps.description: Notices that faster speeds never take more hours, and binary searches for the slowest speed that fits.
look_for: says the hours go down as speed goes up
binary searches between 1 and the largest document
hints: Look at how the total hours change as the speed increases.
If speed 5 fits in the time, could speed 6 ever fail?
The answer is monotonic, so binary search for the smallest speed whose hours fit.

steps.title: Pick the right bounds
steps.description: Searches from 1 to the largest document, and converges on the smallest valid speed.
look_for: upper bound is the largest page count
keeps a valid speed when it fits
hints: Check the smallest and largest speeds your search can try.
Is there any point printing faster than the biggest document?
Search between 1 and the largest document, keeping the boundary when a speed fits.

common_mistakes.description: uses normal division instead of rounding up
common_mistakes.symptom: thinks speed 3 fits for [3, 6, 7, 11] in 8 hours
correct but far too slow when documents have a billion pages

common_mistakes.description: returns the first speed that fits in a search that doesn't keep the minimum
common_mistakes.symptom: gives a valid but too-fast answer

wrap_up_questions: What are the time and space complexity?
How would this change if the printer could switch documents mid-hour?

origin_note: Original. Pattern: binary search on the speed.
